The '''Jenn Aiel''' are an extinct faction of the [[Aiel]]. Unique among Aiel, they did not abandon the [[Way of the Leaf]].{{ref/book|4|25}}{{ref/book|4|26}}

== Appearance ==
They looked exactly like the other Aiel, tall, with light-colored eyes in sun-darkened faces, dressed in the same clothes except for lacking veils. They wore no weapons save for simple belt knives, suitable for work. {{ref/book|4|25}}

==History==
Also see [[Da'shain Aiel]]

===Age of Legends and Breaking===
The Jenn were descended from the Da'shain Aiel of the [[Age of Legends]]. During the [[Breaking of the World]], at the command of [[Solinda|Solinda Sedai]], they were assigned to bring a cache of ''[[angreal]]'', ''[[sa'angreal]]'', and ''[[ter'angreal]]'' to the place of safety that would eventually turn out to be the site of [[Rhuidean]].

===The first split===
The first split among the Da'shain Aiel occurred while the Aiel were traveling in the south of the Westlands. Following a raid, some of them, led by [[Sulwin]], decided to forsake the command of the Aes Sedai and instead seek out the [[Song]], thinking that will bring back the time of peace and prosperity. These people went on to become the ''[[Tuatha'an]]''.{{ref/book|4|25}}

===The second split===
The Aiel who kept to their duty to the Aes Sedai adopted the term "Jenn," meaning "true" in the [[Old Tongue]], after the second split. This split also occurred after a raid.

After some Aiel children were kidnapped, a few young members donned their dust veils and launched an impromptu rescue mission. They were able to save the kidnapped members, but one of them, [[Lewin]], accidentally killed one of the raiders, and the others incapacitated the other raiders. Because of this, even though they had successfully recovered the two women, the men who had committed violence were not allowed to return to the Aiel wagons.

However, [[Lewin]] insisted that he was still Aiel, and followed the Jenn's wagons in order to provide protection. Over time, various other Jenn drifted over to follow them, and their different attitudes eventually gave rise to the various warrior societies, septs and clans among modern Aiel. Eventually a [[Morin|woman]] joined them, forming the core of what would become [[Far Dareis Mai]].{{ref/book|4|25}}

===Last Days===
As time went on, the Aiel population swelled while that of the Jenn dwindled. The Jenn, protected by the "Lost" Aiel (from their perspective), founded the city of [[Rhuidean]] with the help of [[Rhuidean Aes Sedai]] that had rejoined them. The city was originally intended as a cache of [[angreal]], [[sa'angreal]] and [[ter'angreal]] and a haven for Jenn and Aes Sedai; however, there were too few Jenn to make this viable, and so a new purpose was introduced.

A [[Glass columns|huge ''ter'angreal'']] was constructed in the middle of Rhuidean, which would function as a test to select new clan chiefs and [[Wise One]]s. This ''ter'angreal'' showed candidates the true history of the Aiel through their ancestors' eyes in order to teach their leaders about their heritage and prove them to be strong enough to hold it. ''"Who cannot learn, will not live." ''Some, as many as two out of three men, never come out of Rhuidean. The ratio of women who survive is not known.{{ref/book|4|23}}

===Believed extinction===
After Rhuidean was abandoned, it was believed that the Jenn Aiel were completely extinct. However, some did in fact survive and continued a secret part of their purpose, lore, and identity, which was to provide a vessel for something of the [[Creator]].{{ref/book|origins|Nakomi}} By the end of the [[Third Age]], the latest of this line was [[Nakomi]]. She met [[Aviendha]] as she made her way to Rhuidean to test for [[Wise One]], and later met [[Rand al'Thor]] as he left [[Shayol Ghul]] as [[Tarmon Gai'don]] came to an end.{{Ref/book|13|39}}{{Ref/book|14|e}}

==Attitudes towards Jenn==
Today, Aiel prefer not to speak of the Jenn. If they do, it is in hushed tones and with reluctance. They are also referred to as the "clan that is not."
